# Campsite — Style Reference

> Graphite notes on white paper, one green light for whoever's online. Inter at 14px carries the copy on a #ffffff canvas, 1px rings at 10% black draw every edge, and #22c55e lights only when something is live.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Campsite speaks a product-shell marketing language: the home page is assembled from the app's own chrome rather than from conventional marketing components. The canvas is #ffffff, secondary panels step down to #f5f5f5, selected rows and skeleton lines sit on #f0f0f0, and #000000 is reserved for one tiny NEW badge. The chromatic budget is four saturated hues, and none of them sells anything. #22c55e marks live or resolved states, #ef4444 marks alarm, #fd4801 lives only in the logo and one announcement pill, and #fef3c7 highlighter sits behind quoted praise. The paint explosion flanking the hero is photography, not a token. Inter carries everything at 400, 500 and 600, with 14px as the workhorse (29 uses). Headlines are set at 600 and tracked to -1.8px at 64px. The scale climbs by roughly 1.25 to 28.8px, then leaps 2.2× to the display. Shapes split between 9999px pills and 6px, 8px and 12px soft corners. Elevation is a stack of 5%-alpha shadows bound by 1px #0000001a rings. The page reads as a working app laid open on a white desk rather than a landing page selling one.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page body, product window, ringed buttons and post cards. 17 background uses plus the body itself — the single plane everything else is drawn onto. |
| Fog Panel | `#f5f5f5` | `--color-fog-panel` | Feature tile wells, secondary panels and quiet input fields. 9 uses — a one-step tonal drop that groups content without a shadow. |
| Pebble Wash | `#f0f0f0` | `--color-pebble-wash` | Selected sidebar row, active segmented tab, skeleton text bars. 18 uses — the most frequent fill, standing in for "this one is selected". |
| Onyx Badge | `#000000` | `--color-onyx-badge` | The NEW micro-badge in the announcement pill and the window chrome dots' dark counterpart. 2 uses — inverted surface, rationed to a single label. Do not promote it to a button fill. |
| Jet Ink | `#171717` | `--color-jet-ink` | Headlines, body copy, button labels and post titles. 46 uses — a near-black that keeps 64px type from going inky-harsh against pure white. |
| Graphite Caption | `#737373` | `--color-graphite-caption` | Post preview lines, feature descriptions and metadata. 15 uses — the secondary voice, still above 4.5:1 on white. |
| Ash Whisper | `#a3a3a3` | `--color-ash-whisper` | Testimonial body, channel labels, placeholder text and timestamps. 18 uses — tertiary text that recedes so highlighter marks can lead. Do not use it for anything a user must read to act. |
| Smoke Hairline | `#0000001a` | `--color-smoke-hairline` | Card borders, divider lines, testimonial rules and tag outlines. 30 uses at 1px — a translucent edge that adapts to any neutral it sits on. |
| Sprout Signal | `#22c55e` | `--color-sprout-signal` | Join pill, RESOLVED badge and online presence dots. 5 uses — the status color for "live" and "done". Do not promote it to the marketing CTA. |
| Cinder Alarm | `#ef4444` | `--color-cinder-alarm` | Leave-call button, recording indicators and link hover state. 2 fills — the destructive and alarm signal. Keep it off headings and decorative accents. |
| Ember Spark | `#fd4801` | `--color-ember-spark` | App-icon logo and the "founders have joined Notion" pill — brand mark only. Do not use it for buttons, links or data, or it competes with status color. |
| Sunbeam Highlight | `#fef3c7` | `--color-sunbeam-highlight` | Highlighter background behind key testimonial phrases. 3 uses — emphasis by marker pen instead of bold weight. |
| Umber Ink | `#451a03` | `--color-umber-ink` | Text inside Sunbeam highlights and amber labels. 12 uses — a warm brown that keeps highlighted words legible on yellow without reverting to #171717. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Inter — the single voice for headline, interface and prose · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter (Google Fonts, exact match) at 400, 500 and 600. Geist at 400, 500 and 600, which draws at the same stroke weight but slightly narrower, so add 1% width tolerance. Public Sans at 400, 500 and 600, a near match in color with marginally rounder bowls. The site self-hosts Inter via a hashed family name, so nominal and visual weights agree. Match weight for weight.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600
- **Sizes:** 10px, 11px, 12px, 13px, 14px, 15px, 16px, 17px, 18px, 20px, 22.4px, 28.8px, 64px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.2, 1.333, 1.4, 1.429, 1.5, 1.556, 1.625, 1.8
- **Letter spacing:** -1.8px at 64px, -0.5px at 28.8px, -0.4px at 22.4px, +0.275px at 11px uppercase, 0px at every other size
- **Role:** Weight 400 accounts for 58 elements and 600 for only 14, so semibold is rationed to headlines and badges. Most of the page is set at app-reading weight. The middle of the scale steps 14 → 17 → 22.4 → 28.8, close to a Major Third (1.25) and a Perfect Fourth (1.333). The display then skips two conventional steps and jumps 2.2× to 64px, so the H1 behaves like a cover line above a page of interface-sized type. The negative tracking at display sizes is conventional for Inter. What stands out is that it stops at 22.4px: everything below that size is left at default spacing, exactly as the app renders it.

### ui-monospace — system mono for counts and technical tallies · `--font-ui-monospace`

- **Substitute:** Geist Mono at 400 and 600. JetBrains Mono at 400 and 600, which draws a touch heavier, so drop 600 to 500 at 11px. IBM Plex Mono at 400 and 600.
- **Weights:** 400, 600
- **Sizes:** 11px, 12px, 16px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** -0.55px at 11px, 0px at 12px and 16px
- **Role:** Mono appears in 7 elements, as comment counts, reaction tallies and code fragments inside the product mockup. It is never used for marketing copy. The -0.55px tracking at 11px (-0.05em) tightens digits so a count like "34" sits as a compact token beside a 14px preview line. Mono here signals machine-counted data, a technical register that is deliberately kept inside the screenshot.

### Emoji — color glyphs as channel and reaction icons · `--font-emoji`

- **Substitute:** Apple Color Emoji, Noto Color Emoji and Twemoji, each at 400. Color glyphs ignore weight, so the number only sets fallback metrics.
- **Weights:** 500, 600
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px
- **Line height:** 1.0
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 12px and 14px
- **Role:** Emoji take the place of an icon set for channels (🧪 Product, 🎉, 🔥) and reactions, set at 12px with a 1.0 line height so they align to the caption baseline. This is the system's only sanctioned source of incidental color inside the UI. It is small, user-chosen and content rather than chrome, which is why it does not count against the chromatic budget.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter | 600 | 10px | 1.0 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter | 400 | 12px | 1.333 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 14px | 1.429 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 400 | 16px | 1.8 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter | 400 | 17px | 1.625 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter | 500 | 22.4px | 1.5 | -0.4px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading | Inter | 600 | 28.8px | 1.2 | -0.5px | `--text-heading` |
| display | Inter | 600 | 64px | 1.0 | -1.8px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every marketing heading in Inter weight 600 with negative tracking, -1.8px at 64px and -0.5px at 28.8px — headlines should read as product titles scaled up, not as display-face posters.
- Default all interface text and small prose to 14px weight 400 at a 1.429 line height — it is the most-used style (29 elements), and matching the app's reading size is the thesis.
- Draw edges with 1px #0000001a, and lift objects with the md stack at 5% alpha per layer — the translucent ring adapts to #ffffff, #f5f5f5 and #f0f0f0 without a second border color.
- Restrict #22c55e to live, online and resolved states, and treat that restriction as non-negotiable — the green carries meaning only because it is used for nothing else.
- Give marketing-level controls 9999px corners and in-product controls 6px corners — the radius tells the reader which layer they are touching.
- Separate sections by 144px and center each heading in a 672px column above its demo — the generous gap frames each UI vignette like a specimen on a white plate.
- Emphasize quoted praise with a #fef3c7 highlight and #451a03 text instead of weight 600 — annotation reads as a real reader's mark, while bold reads as ad copy.

### Don't

- Don't paint the "Open app" button #fd4801 or #22c55e to "boost conversion" — color in this system is status, never salesmanship, and a brand-filled CTA collapses the grayscale-chrome thesis.
- Don't use #fd4801 for links, icons or hover states — the ember belongs to the logo and one news pill, and spreading it turns a signature into noise.
- Don't add a conventional `0 20px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` card shadow — the deepest drop in the system is the lg popover at 10% alpha, so anything heavier makes the demo look pasted on.
- Don't bump body text to 18px for "readability" — 14px and 16px are the app's real sizes, and enlarging them breaks the 1:1 fidelity between page and product.
- Don't introduce weight 700 for headings — 600 is the ceiling (14 uses), and heavier strokes at 64px tip the page from editorial calm into SaaS shouting.
- Don't round cards to 16px or 24px — cards cap at 12px, and only the outer 18px frame exceeds it, so softer corners blur the line between the window and its contents.
- Don't sample the orange-red paint splash into UI tokens — it is photographic decoration outside the frame, and tokenizing it would give the chrome a second accent family.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- secondary surface: #f5f5f5 (Fog Panel)
- selected state: #f0f0f0 (Pebble Wash)
- primary text: #171717 (Jet Ink)
- secondary text: #737373 (Graphite Caption)
- hairline: #0000001a (Smoke Hairline)
- live status: #22c55e (Sprout Signal)
- primary action: no distinct CTA color

**Color in Data**

Charts stay neutral, with #f0f0f0 tracks, #a3a3a3 secondary bars and #171717 for the focal series. Only a series that represents a live or positive state may use #22c55e as a solid fill. #fd4801 and #ef4444 are not data colors.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button labeled "Open app": an anchor with background #ffffff, text #171717, Inter 14px weight 500, line height 20px, height 30px, padding 0 10px, border none and border-radius 9999px. Apply box-shadow `0px 1px 1px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), 0px 2px 2px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), 0px 0px 0px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.06), inset 0px 1px 0px 0px #ffffff, inset 0px 1px 2px 1px #ffffff, inset 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)`. On hover, change the background to #f5f5f5. Do not add any saturated color.

2. Build a hero section on #ffffff inside a 1280px container, with all content centered. At the top, place a pill: #ffffff background, sm ring shadow, 9999px radius, padding 0 4px, Inter 13px weight 500 #171717 text. Inside the pill, a #000000 NEW badge (10px weight 600 uppercase #ffffff, padding 0 6px, 9999px radius) sits before the label. Below the pill with an 8px gap, place a #fd4801 pill with #ffffff 13px weight 500 text. Then, 48px below, a two-line H1 in Inter 64px weight 600, line height 64px, letter-spacing -1.8px, #171717. Add 16px of space, then a lede in Inter 22.4px weight 500, line height 33.6px, letter-spacing -0.4px, #171717, max-width 672px. Finish 48px below with a product window card: #ffffff, 1px solid #0000001a, 12px radius, five-layer md shadow at rgba(0,0,0,0.05).

3. Build a feature row with two columns and a 16px gap. On the left, a tile with background #f5f5f5, 1px solid #0000001a, border-radius 8px and padding 32px 12px. It contains a white card (#ffffff, 8px radius, padding 12px, md shadow) showing a 16px outline icon and the text "Show summary" in Inter 14px weight 500 #171717 over "34 comments" in 14px weight 400 #737373. On the right, a title in Inter 16px weight 600 #171717 and, 4px below it, a description in Inter 16px weight 400 #737373 at line height 1.8, max-width 384px.

4. Build a navigation bar: a transparent, non-sticky row 64px tall, inside a 1280px container with 24px horizontal padding. On the left, a 24px square logo with a #fd4801 fill and 6px radius. On the right, a flex row with a 24px gap containing "Blog" and "Changelog" in Inter 14px weight 400 #171717, followed by the white-ring "Open app" pill from prompt 1. Add no border-bottom and no background.

5. Build a testimonial block: a 1px solid #0000001a left border, padding-left 12px, max-width 672px. The quote is Inter 17px weight 400, line height 1.625, color #a3a3a3. Wrap the key clause in a span with background #fef3c7 and color #451a03. Below it with a 12px gap, add a 24px round avatar (9999px radius) and the name line in Inter 16px weight 400 #a3a3a3, with 8px between avatar and text.

Border-radius is 9999px, padding 0 10px, height 30px, with Inter at 14px weight 500 and the full sm shadow (two 8% lifts plus white inset highlights). Convention gives the primary action a brand fill. Here it gets none, and is distinguished only by its ring and its far-right slot in the nav, so the button reads as app chrome rather than an advertisement.

### Soft Button — Ringed (Secondary)

**Role:** In-product actions inside demo mockups

The 6px workhorse. "Join channel" and similar in-app buttons use background #ffffff, text #171717, no border, border-radius 6px, padding 0 10px and height 40px in the call card (32px for icon variants). Type is Inter at 14px weight 500, with the same sm ring-and-inset shadow as the primary pill. The radius is the only difference between the two buttons. Pills mean "leave the page" and 6px corners mean "act inside the product", a deliberate split that keeps the marketing layer and the app layer legible in one view.

### Segmented Tab — Ghost and Active

**Role:** Inbox filters and view switches

Flat, fill-only selection. The ghost state ("Inbox") has a transparent background, #171717 text, no border and no shadow. The active state ("Follow up") takes a 6% black tint that renders as #f0f0f0 on white. Both use border-radius 6px, padding 0 10px, height 30px and Inter at 14px weight 500. Selection is shown by a tonal wash rather than an underline or a colored pill, the same Pebble Wash used on the selected sidebar row. A single fill therefore means "you are here" throughout the system.

### Status Pill — Green Join

**Role:** Live-call entry inside the mockup

The one colored button. "Join" uses background #22c55e, text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 9999px, padding 0 10px, height 32px, Inter at 14px weight 500, and no shadow. It is the system outlier: the only filled saturated button on the page, and it exists only inside the product screenshot. That placement is allowed because green here is status, not persuasion. It says "a call is live right now". Reuse this spec for presence-driven actions only, never for signup or pricing.

### Announcement Stack — NEW Badge and Ember Pill

**Role:** News above the hero headline

Two stacked capsules. The upper pill uses #ffffff with #171717 text at Inter 13px weight 500, padding 0 4px, radius 9999px and the sm ring shadow. It holds a #000000 NEW badge with #ffffff text at 10px weight 600 uppercase, radius 9999px and padding 0 6px, followed by a 12px arrow icon. Below it, a pill filled #fd4801 carries #ffffff 13px weight 500 text. This is the only shape besides the logo that Ember Spark may fill. The exception is allowed because it is news, temporary and positioned above the fold rather than inside the system.

### Navigation Bar

**Role:** Static top bar with minimal links

Transparent, unpinned, three-item. The bar sits on #ffffff with no fill, border or shadow, roughly 64px tall (estimated), and scrolls away with the page instead of sticking. On the left is the 24px Ember Spark app-icon logo with a 6px radius (estimated). On the right, "Blog" and "Changelog" are set in Inter 14px weight 400 #171717 with 24px gaps (estimated), followed by the white-ring "Open app" pill. Convention adds Pricing, Features and a colored signup button. Removing them makes the nav read as a window toolbar.

### Product Window Frame

**Role:** Hero screenshot and main content card

The page's center of gravity. The frame is a full app window on #ffffff with a 1px #0000001a border, border-radius 12px and the md five-layer 5% shadow, spanning most of the 1280px container. A #f5f5f5 sidebar runs left with 14px weight 400 rows, and the selected row is filled #f0f0f0 at 6px radius. The center feed carries a 28.8px weight 600 "Home" title, and a presence column runs right with 24px avatars and #22c55e online dots. It is the largest card on the page and is drawn exactly like the product, so the demo is the argument.

### Post Row Card

**Role:** Single-post preview under section headings

A stacked-paper feed item. Background #ffffff, 1px #0000001a border, border-radius 12px, padding 12px, and the subtle 0px 1px 2px shadow. Two offset hairline cards peek beneath it to suggest a pile of posts. The 40px round avatar sits left, then a title in Inter 15px weight 500 #171717, then a preview line at 14px weight 400 #737373 led by a 12px mono comment count. A channel tag closes the row on the right. It is the atomic unit of Campsite's content model, shown at 1:1 scale.

### Feature Tile — Fog Well

**Role:** Illustration plate beside feature text

Recessed, framed, wordless. The tile is #f5f5f5 with a 1px #0000001a border, border-radius 8px and padding 12px. It holds a white inner card at 8px radius with the md shadow, or a bottom-flush strip whose corners are 7px. That 7px is deliberate: 8px minus the 1px border, so inner and outer curves stay concentric. Feature copy sits right of the tile in a 16px weight 600 title and #737373 16px weight 400 description at 1.8 line height. This is a two-column pattern that substitutes mini-UI for icons.

### Channel Tag Pill

**Role:** Channel label on post rows

Outlined micro-label. The tag has a transparent background, a 1px #0000001a border, border-radius 9999px and padding 2px 8px. It contains a 12px emoji followed by Inter 12px weight 400 #a3a3a3 text ("Product", "Stripe", "Q4 Growth"). There is no fill and no hue: the emoji carries the only color, chosen by users rather than the system. Tags are meant to be scanned, not clicked, so they sit at tertiary contrast, deliberately quieter than the #737373 preview text beside them.

### Resolved Badge

**Role:** Completed-state marker on posts

Solid status capsule. The badge is #22c55e with #ffffff text, border-radius 9999px and padding 4px 8px. It shows a 12px check-circle icon followed by Inter 10px weight 600 uppercase text with 0px tracking. It shares its fill exactly with the Join pill, which keeps the green vocabulary to one hex for every positive state. Uppercase 10px at 600 is the smallest text on the page and is reserved for state labels. The badge works as punctuation rather than decoration.

### Highlighted Testimonial

**Role:** Social proof between feature sections

Marker-pen emphasis. The quote has no card. It is indented behind a 1px #0000001a left rule with 12px padding-left, set in Inter 17px weight 400 #a3a3a3 at 1.625 line height. The key phrase is wrapped in a #fef3c7 background with #451a03 text and a 2px radius-free mark. Attribution follows: a 24px round avatar and a 16px weight 400 #a3a3a3 name line. Conventional testimonials go bold or large. This one dims the whole quote and lights a single clause, the way a reader would annotate it.

### Mention Popover

**Role:** @-mention and backlink picker demo

The most elevated object. The popover is #ffffff with border-radius 8px, padding 6px and the lg shadow (inset hairline plus 2px, 4px/12px and 8px/20px drops), slightly rotated in the illustration. Group labels are set at 12px weight 500 #737373 ("Posts", "People"), and rows are 14px weight 400 #171717 with a 12px doc icon or 24px avatar. A 1px #0000001a divider separates the groups. It is the only lg-shadow surface, which reserves deep elevation for transient menus.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every marketing heading in Inter weight 600 with negative tracking, -1.8px at 64px and -0.5px at 28.8px — headlines should read as product titles scaled up, not as display-face posters.
- Default all interface text and small prose to 14px weight 400 at a 1.429 line height — it is the most-used style (29 elements), and matching the app's reading size is the thesis.
- Draw edges with 1px #0000001a, and lift objects with the md stack at 5% alpha per layer — the translucent ring adapts to #ffffff, #f5f5f5 and #f0f0f0 without a second border color.
- Restrict #22c55e to live, online and resolved states, and treat that restriction as non-negotiable — the green carries meaning only because it is used for nothing else.
- Give marketing-level controls 9999px corners and in-product controls 6px corners — the radius tells the reader which layer they are touching.
- Separate sections by 144px and center each heading in a 672px column above its demo — the generous gap frames each UI vignette like a specimen on a white plate.
- Emphasize quoted praise with a #fef3c7 highlight and #451a03 text instead of weight 600 — annotation reads as a real reader's mark, while bold reads as ad copy.

### Don't

- Don't paint the "Open app" button #fd4801 or #22c55e to "boost conversion" — color in this system is status, never salesmanship, and a brand-filled CTA collapses the grayscale-chrome thesis.
- Don't use #fd4801 for links, icons or hover states — the ember belongs to the logo and one news pill, and spreading it turns a signature into noise.
- Don't add a conventional `0 20px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` card shadow — the deepest drop in the system is the lg popover at 10% alpha, so anything heavier makes the demo look pasted on.
- Don't bump body text to 18px for "readability" — 14px and 16px are the app's real sizes, and enlarging them breaks the 1:1 fidelity between page and product.
- Don't introduce weight 700 for headings — 600 is the ceiling (14 uses), and heavier strokes at 64px tip the page from editorial calm into SaaS shouting.
- Don't round cards to 16px or 24px — cards cap at 12px, and only the outer 18px frame exceeds it, so softer corners blur the line between the window and its contents.
- Don't sample the orange-red paint splash into UI tokens — it is photographic decoration outside the frame, and tokenizing it would give the chrome a second accent family.

## Imagery

The page uses product screenshots rebuilt as live HTML rather than flat image captures: the hero app window, the post row, the feature tiles and the mention popover are all real DOM with real tokens. Photography is limited to round avatars at 40px, 24px and 22px, cropped with 9999px radius and no border. Square logo tiles ("P.", "S") use a 4px radius. Icons are 1.5px-stroke outline glyphs in #171717 or #737373 at 12px to 16px, with emoji standing in for colored icons. The one loud image is a pair of orange-and-red paint explosions bleeding off the left and right of the hero window. They are decorative only, not system tokens, and their colors are mockup-internal. Handwritten script annotations with hand-drawn arrows ("See a real post", "automatic backlinks") are embedded images, not a font. The narrative is energy kept outside the frame and calm inside it.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1280px container, with headings and copy narrowed to a 672px centered column (measured text blocks run 608px). The page has 7 sections separated by 144px gaps. The hero stacks the announcement pills, a two-line 64px headline, a 22.4px lede and then the full-width product window flanked by paint splashes. Following sections repeat one rhythm: a centered 28.8px heading, one UI vignette, then a highlighted testimonial. The features section switches to two columns, with a fog tile left and title and description right, stacked vertically. There is no pricing grid and no logo row. The nav is static, transparent and about 64px tall (estimated), with the logo left and Blog, Changelog and "Open app" right. The footer is a minimal single row. At 375px, drop the display to the 28.8px heading size, set section gaps to 64px and stack feature tiles above their text. Overall density: spacious.

**Quick Color Reference**

**Example Component Prompts**

2. Build a hero section on #ffffff inside a 1280px container, with all content centered. At the top, place a pill: #ffffff background, sm ring shadow, 9999px radius, padding 0 4px, Inter 13px weight 500 #171717 text. Inside the pill, a #000000 NEW badge (10px weight 600 uppercase #ffffff, padding 0 6px, 9999px radius) sits before the label. Below the pill with an 8px gap, place a #fd4801 pill with #ffffff 13px weight 500 text. Then, 48px below, a two-line H1 in Inter 64px weight 600, line height 64px, letter-spacing -1.8px, #171717. On the right, a title in Inter 16px weight 600 #171717 and, 4px below it, a description in Inter 16px weight 400 #737373 at line height 1.8, max-width 384px.

## Status-Only Color

The discipline is that every saturated hue must answer the question "what state is this in?" #22c55e means live or resolved, #ef4444 means alarm or leave, and #fef3c7 means a reader marked this. The ember #fd4801 is the brand's signature and sits outside the state system entirely. What breaks the discipline is any hue used to attract attention for its own sake: a green CTA, a red heading, an orange icon set, a gradient section band. To extend the system, attach every new color to a new state, such as a blue for "unread" restricted to a 6px dot. Keep the fill out of buttons, headings and backgrounds. If a proposed color has no state to name, it does not ship.

## Product-As-Page

The site's thesis is that marketing chrome and app chrome are the same material: 14px Inter, 6px corners, 1px #0000001a rings and #f0f0f0 selection fills, with the hero rendered as a real window instead of a framed screenshot. Conventional SaaS pages invent a separate marketing kit with bigger radii, gradient cards and icon grids. Campsite refuses to. The discipline breaks the moment a section uses a component that could not exist inside the app, such as an illustrated feature card, a three-column icon grid or a pricing table with a shaded "popular" column. To extend the page, build each new section as a cropped piece of product UI on a #f5f5f5 well. Keep the 28.8px heading as the only marketing-scale element per section.

## Annotation Over Emphasis

Campsite emphasizes by marking, not by enlarging. Testimonials dim the entire quote to #a3a3a3 and light a single clause with #fef3c7 behind #451a03. Handwritten arrows label demo details, and weight never exceeds 600 anywhere on the page. This inverts the conventional landing-page habit of bold pull quotes and oversized stats. The approach breaks if highlighted text also goes bold, if two highlights appear in one quote, or if the script annotations multiply into a decorative motif. To extend it, allow at most one highlight per block and one handwritten note per section. Keep the surrounding copy at tertiary contrast so the mark carries the hierarchy alone.

## Similar Brands

- **Campsite** — shares Linear's grayscale product-as-hero approach, with Inter at 600 and live UI instead of illustrations. Linear runs dark while Campsite stays on #ffffff.
- **Campsite** — shares Twist's async-thread category and post-not-chat positioning. Twist leans on a colored brand UI where Campsite rations color to status.
- **Campsite** — shares Notion's off-black ink on white, 1px translucent hairlines and highlighter-style emphasis. This is no accident, as its founders joined Notion.
- **Campsite** — shares Vercel's #171717-on-white palette and ring-in-shadow button construction. Vercel uses sharper corners and Geist where Campsite keeps 9999px pills and Inter.
